name: Prize crossword No 26,268
preamble: Eight clues lack a definition; their solutions are of a kind.

entries.clue: What's that about cutting overtures of Cats, Follies and Oliver? (4)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in turned about, facing the other way, so EH is read backwards
indicatorNotes.cutting: the reversed word cuts between the two initials, sitting inside them
indicatorNotes.overtures of: an overture opens a show, so each named show gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: what you say when you didn't catch something

annotation.surface: A theatregoer puzzled over a revue that chops the openings of three famous musicals.
annotation.walkthrough: Oliver looks like the third musical, but he is Jamie Oliver, the TV cook; only Cats and Follies lend initials.
annotation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a celebrity chef, so Oliver is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Recurring action of mouse with no tail, put in clay moulding (8)

indicatorNotes.with no tail: a word's tail is its end, so the word loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.put in: to put something in is to place it inside, here inside the reshaped clay
indicatorNotes.moulding: clay being moulded is squeezed into a new shape, so its letters change order

blocks.note: first part of the rearranged CLAY

blocks.clueFragment: action of mouse with no tail
blocks.note: a mouse's action is a CLICK; lose the final K

annotation.surface: A potter keeps clicking away at a lump of clay, turning it over and over.
annotation.walkthrough: The mouse is the computer kind, whose action is a click.
annotation.definitionFit: Something cyclical comes round again and again, which is recurring.

entries.clue: Element of metal on glass (4)

indicatorNotes.Element of: an element is one component part, so the answer is a part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: A chemistry note about a metallic element coated onto glass.
annotation.walkthrough: One of eight unclued theme answers: each goes before ISLAND, here Long Island in New York, and the clue gives wordplay only.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Long Island is the island east of New York City.

entries.clue: NEC moves assimilated by player (Bird) (8)

indicatorNotes.moves: the letters of NEC shift about
indicatorNotes.assimilated by: taken into the body of the other word

annotation.surface: A performer called Bird takes on board the moves shown at the NEC, Birmingham's exhibition centre.
annotation.walkthrough: The brackets make Bird look like the player's name; it is the definition. The NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham.
annotation.definitionFit: The accentor is a small songbird; the dunnock is the best-known one.

entries.clue: Amphitheatre seating in present times needs protection of beam (6)

indicatorNotes.needs protection of: the outer word wraps round and shields the inner one

blocks.note: Anno Domini, the era we live in

annotation.surface: Modern stadium seats need a sturdy beam to shelter under.
annotation.walkthrough: Beam reads as a girder in the surface; here it is the verb, a broad smile.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gradin, from French for a step, names the stepped rows of seats rising round an arena.

entries.clue: Special faculty associated with publicity and moon furrow footwear (10)

blocks.note: a rille is a long channel on the moon's surface

annotation.surface: A psychic promoting a special shoe that leaves furrows on the moon.
annotation.walkthrough: RILLE is a term from lunar geology, rarely met outside crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: An espadrille is a canvas shoe with a rope sole.

entries.clue: Worked more, by being in development (6)

indicatorNotes.Worked: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: Someone putting in extra hours on a project still under development.
annotation.walkthrough: Being is the noun, a creature, not the verb it seems to lean on.
annotation.definitionFit: An embryo is a living being in its earliest stage of development.

entries.clue: A stretch in Oxford's dual central prison (4)

indicatorNotes.central: the central part of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: the middle two letters of prISon

annotation.surface: Doing a stretch in an Oxford jail, a double sentence served in the middle of the prison.
annotation.walkthrough: A stretch is a jail term in the surface; here it is a stretch of river.
annotation.definitionFit: The Isis is the name given to the Thames where it flows through Oxford.

entries.clue: Heard from one who's resigned from rustic dance house? (3-2)

blocks.note: a hey is an old country dance

annotation.surface: Someone who has quit their job is overheard at a barn dance.
annotation.walkthrough: Resigned means accepting what can't be helped, not leaving a job.
annotation.definitionFit: Hey-ho is the sigh of someone putting up with things.

entries.clue: Speed of light? Uncommonly smartish! (9)

indicatorNotes.Uncommonly: letters arranged in an uncommon way are out of their usual order

blocks.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

annotation.surface: A remark that something fairly quick is unusually so for light.
annotation.walkthrough: One of eight unclued theme answers: each goes before ISLAND, here Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean, and the clue gives wordplay only.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Christmas Island is an Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.

entries.clue: Made ornamental horse sound on eating too much? (9)

indicatorNotes.sound: take what the word sounds like

blocks.note: a filly is a young female horse

annotation.surface: A horse that has been dressed up in finery makes noises while gorging itself.
annotation.walkthrough: Horse sound suggests a neigh; it means a horse word as it sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: To filigree is to decorate with delicate ornamental tracery.

entries.clue: Hanging arranged by a saint (5)

blocks.note: the abbreviation printed on sheet music

annotation.surface: A tapestry has been hung up by a holy person.
annotation.walkthrough: ARR is the music abbreviation for arranged by.
annotation.definitionFit: An arras is a wall hanging, like the one Polonius hides behind in Hamlet.

entries.clue: Lack variety in touch display type (7)

indicatorNotes.variety: 'lack variety' read as LACK varied: a variety of the word, its letters in another order
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the reshaped letters inside the next word

blocks.note: a touch, as in a bit of

annotation.surface: A complaint that a touchscreen gadget offers too few kinds of display.
annotation.walkthrough: Touch reads as touchscreen next to display; it is just a small amount.
annotation.definitionFit: A backlit screen is lit from behind, a common kind of display.

entries.clue: Simple language when entered in pen (5)

indicatorNotes.entered in: something entered in a pen is written into it, so AS goes inside BIC

annotation.surface: Plain words written down in ink.
annotation.walkthrough: BASIC is an early beginner's programming language, hence simple.
annotation.definitionFit: BASIC stands for Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code, a simple language.

entries.clue: Utilising flexible capacitance of tongues (10)

indicatorNotes.flexible: the letters bend into a new order

annotation.surface: An engineer puts the variable capacitance of some device to use.
annotation.walkthrough: C is the symbol for capacitance in physics.
annotation.definitionFit: Linguistic means relating to languages, or tongues.

entries.clue: Absence of right traditional music (7)

annotation.surface: A lament that proper traditional music is missing.
annotation.walkthrough: One of eight unclued theme answers: each goes before ISLAND, here Norfolk Island in the Pacific, not the English county.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Norfolk Island is an Australian territory in the South Pacific.

entries.clue: My young friend's tease act (5)

annotation.surface: Someone describes a youngster's prank as a put-on.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is the verb has, not a possessive: KIDDO has KID then DO.
annotation.definitionFit: Kiddo is a familiar way of addressing a young person.

entries.clue: Old writers' gathering — also abstract noun (5)

indicatorNotes.abstract: the letters are drawn out and rearranged

annotation.surface: A grammar note: a literary circle, which is also an abstract noun.
annotation.walkthrough: Abstract noun is a grammar phrase; the two words split, one scrambling ALSO and the other giving N.
annotation.definitionFit: Salons were gatherings of writers and thinkers, especially in 18th-century Paris.

entries.clue: Reverse hesitation in speech (3)

blocks.note: R marks reverse on a gear stick

annotation.surface: A speaker backtracks, stumbling over the words.
annotation.walkthrough: Reverse looks like an instruction to turn UM round; it is just R. One of eight unclued theme answers: Rum is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Rum is one of the Small Isles off western Scotland.

entries.clue: Spotted ring in a muscle abnormality (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the ring sits in the muscle, so O joins those letters
indicatorNotes.abnormality: an abnormal muscle is not in its normal form, so its letters are out of their normal order

annotation.surface: A doctor notes a spotted ring inside a malformed muscle.
annotation.walkthrough: The O joins A MUSCLE before the whole is rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Maculose means spotted, from Latin macula, a spot.

entries.clue: Composed clue: clue finally replaced by one with depth, easy to understand (5)

indicatorNotes.Composed: the letters are put together afresh
indicatorNotes.replaced by: swap the one piece for the other

blocks.note: last letter of clue, to be removed

annotation.surface: A setter describes how a clue got clearer: rewritten with a deeper ending.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged CLUE must end in E so that swapping that E for ID works.
annotation.definitionFit: Lucid means clearly expressed and easy to understand.

entries.clue: Heel rest with copper insert as fancy twist (8)

indicatorNotes.insert: an insert is a piece set into something else, so copper goes into the rest

blocks.note: a heel is a rotter, a cur

annotation.surface: A footrest for the heel has a decorative copper twist set into it.
annotation.walkthrough: Heel rest looks like one footrest; the two words work separately, and heel means a scoundrel.
annotation.definitionFit: A curlicue is a decorative curl or twist in a design or handwriting.

entries.clue: Make it easier to bear to go to work? (7)

blocks.note: the legal sense: what a governor does to a prison sentence, reducing it

annotation.surface: Someone wonders what would make the trip to the office more bearable.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is legal: to commute a sentence is to reduce it.
annotation.definitionFit: Commuting a sentence lightens it; commuting is also the daily trip to work.

entries.clue: Unclear about direction (6)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in turned about, so DIM faces the other way

annotation.surface: Someone is unsure which way to go.
annotation.walkthrough: One of eight unclued theme answers: each goes before ISLAND, here Midway Island in the Pacific, site of the 1942 battle.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Midway is a Pacific atoll, often called the Midway Islands.

entries.clue: What's comforting about time (6)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in around, so EASER surrounds the T

annotation.surface: A question about what makes time pass comfortably.
annotation.walkthrough: One of eight unclued theme answers: each goes before ISLAND, here Easter Island in the Pacific, home of the stone heads.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Easter Island (Rapa Nui) is the Pacific island famous for its moai statues.

entries.clue: So long as eastern city follows cult hero (7)

indicatorNotes.follows: what follows comes after, so E and RIO are placed after CHE

annotation.surface: A travel note: as long as the eastern city trails the hero-worship.
annotation.walkthrough: So long as looks like one phrase meaning provided that; so long is the goodbye and as is the link.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheerio and so long are both informal goodbyes.

entries.clue: Hot destination was in possession of drugs (5)

annotation.surface: A traveller to a hot holiday spot is caught carrying drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot destination looks like a sunny resort; it is hell.
annotation.definitionFit: Hades is the underworld, a hot place to end up.

entries.clue: Bush left out (4)

indicatorNotes.left out: L, the abbreviation for left, is omitted from the word

blocks.note: HOLLY, a bush, loses one L

annotation.surface: A shrub has been left outside.
annotation.walkthrough: Bush left out reads like a politician excluded. One of eight unclued theme answers: Holy Island is Lindisfarne, off the Northumberland coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Holy Island is Lindisfarne in north-east England.

entries.clue: Make serious film, yes? No, funny (9)

indicatorNotes.funny: funny in the sense of peculiar: the letters are behaving oddly, out of order

annotation.surface: A director hesitates over making a serious film, then decides on a comedy.
annotation.walkthrough: Funny is the anagram indicator, sitting at the end after the punctuation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the -ify ending means make, and solemn means serious.

entries.clue: Greek character, one who once defended uprising? (4)

indicatorNotes.uprising: in a down entry a word rising up is read from bottom to top, so KC reverses

blocks.note: King's Counsel, the old title for a senior barrister

annotation.surface: A Greek figure who once defended a rebellion.
annotation.walkthrough: A KC is a senior barrister, King's Counsel; once, because the title was QC for the whole reign of Elizabeth II. One of eight unclued theme answers: Muck is one of the Small Isles off western Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: Unclued theme entry: Muck is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides.

entries.clue: Couple authorise interrupting you once (4)

annotation.surface: A pair give their blessing, cutting in on an old-fashioned address.
annotation.walkthrough: Couple is the verb, to join together.
annotation.definitionFit: To yoke is to couple or join, as oxen are yoked together.

entries.clue: A feature of woodland, meadow and narrow borders of spinneys (9)

blocks.note: a fine line is a narrow one
first and last letters of spinneys

indicatorNotes.borders of: the edge letters of the word

annotation.surface: A nature guide lists the features of woods, fields and the thin edges of copses.
annotation.walkthrough: A spinney is a small wood; only its outer letters count.
annotation.definitionFit: Woodland is marked by being full of leaves, its leafiness.

entries.clue: Stop boat leaking and one breaks bad luck? (5)

indicatorNotes.breaks: one breaking into something gets inside it, so A goes into the other letters
indicatorNotes.bad: bad luck here is LUCK gone bad, spoilt out of its proper order

annotation.surface: A sailor, cursing bad luck, tries to stop the boat from leaking.
annotation.walkthrough: The A sits inside the rearranged LUCK after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Caulking seals the seams of a boat so it stops leaking.
